source.title: La Primavera / Spring, RV 269 — I. Allegro

voices.name: Organ and cello bass line (not realised continuo)

bars.description: Eighth-note pickup (bar 0), then bars 1–82 once in written order. Echoes and returning refrains are written out; no repeat traversal is inserted. Only movement I is used.

end.basis: Fixed-common-reference pitch profiles distinguish a faint tonal decay from the global overlay’s display floor: E2 remains roughly 60 feature-dB above its adjacent semitone bins at 212.6 s, while G-sharp4/E5 also remain narrowly pitched through about 212.8 s. E2 then falls approximately 60–70 feature-dB below its final-chord reference by 213.6–213.8 s. Retain a 213.78 s pitched-decay display boundary, not an unsupported 210.6 s truncation. These are 20-log10 cached-feature ratios, not acoustic SPL or a measured bow release; the original whole-file RMS endpoint remains in the checks.

endpoints.basis: The genuine eighth-note pickup is the joint source-pitch rise near 0.28 s. The final E-major arrival is near 209.0 s, where E2/E5/G-sharp4 jointly replace the preceding B2/F-sharp5 dominant through 208.5 s. The stronger E/G-sharp energy around 205.5 s is an earlier cadence figure and must not collapse the remaining written notes. Pitch-band inspection, not closest-detector selection; no aural review is claimed.

provenance: The archive’s spring-score.mid is movement I only, with named source staves solo, violinone, violintwo, viola and cello. spring-score-1.mid and spring-score-2.mid are movements II and III and are not used.

The source’s Organo e Violoncello part supplies one written bass line plus figured-bass symbols. No realised continuo pitches or separately inferred double-bass voice are invented. The source maintainer is explicitly Anonymous.
Source MIDI contains 3173 note attacks over 328.5 quarter-note units; the pickup is labelled bar 0, followed by 82 complete 4/4 bars.
